correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite G=K_{n1,...,nk}, k>=3 with >=2 nonsingleton blocks and coordinate Euclidean stable-set polytope, a facet is coordinate x_ia=0 or maximal-clique sum selected x<=1. Facet-pair ridge criterion follows by block-maximum saturation: all LL; LU unless lower selected in nonsingleton; UU iff one block differs. Their normal inner products yield right, acute arccos(1/sqrt(k)), and obtuse pi-arccos((k-1)/k) classes. With C=prod(n_i!)/(N-2)!, Dirichlet block maxima and induced Jacobians 1,sqrt(k),sqrt(k-1),sqrt(2k-1) yield exact totals C((k*k-s)/2+(k-s)sqrt(k)), Cs sqrt(k-1), C(k-s)sqrt(2k-1)/2. For k=5,s=3, right=(11+2sqrt5)C, acute=6C, obtuse=3C; angles pi/2-arctan(1/2) and pi/2+2arctan(1/2) give cancellation exactly and V_(N-2)=(5+sqrt5/2)C under Euclidean Steiner convention. Independently enumerated every ridge and used affine Euclidean hull volumes for profiles (1,1,1,2,2), (1,1,2,2), (1,2,2), agreeing by class to numerical tolerance; all-size proof is analytic Dirichlet identity.

value.rationale: The discovery that normalized Euclidean ridge measures of a variable-size multipartite polytope depend only on k and the singleton count is a natural geometric structural invariant, with nontrivial exact sharp five-partite cancellation and an intrinsic-volume corollary. Metric ridge areas cannot be inferred from a combinatorial f-vector/angle census alone, and no unmotivated graph slice is required.
